prompt: Pin down the difference between getMethods and getDeclaredMethods: list the public methods a class exposes, the methods it declares itself, and the public ones it only inherits. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: getMethods and getDeclaredMethods answer two different questions: what can a caller reach, and what did this class actually write. That is why a private method shows up in the declared list but never in the public one, and why an inherited public method shows up in the public list but never in the declared one. Everything inherits from Object, so getMethods always drags in toString, equals, hashCode and the rest -- filtering on getDeclaringClass() != Object.class keeps the answer about your own hierarchy. A TreeSet gives sorting and de-duplication in one step, which matters because an overridden method can appear twice in getMethods once bridge methods are involved.
hints: Both listing methods have the same shape: loop over the array, add method.getName() to a TreeSet<String>, then return new ArrayList<>(that set).
method.getDeclaringClass() tells you which class actually defines a method; compare it with Object.class to filter the inherited built-ins.
inheritedPublicNames does not need reflection of its own -- call your other two methods and keep the public names the declared list does not contain.
